title: Research Methods: Experiment, Correlation, Questionnaire, Interview, Observation
summary: Experimental method; correlational method; questionnaire; interview; observation; strengths and limitations of each.
objectives: Define experiment, correlation, questionnaire, interview and observation.
Explain why correlation does not imply causation.
Compare strengths and limitations of each data collection method.
revision: Experiment manipulates IV to measure DV; correlation measures relationship (not causation); questionnaire/interview/observation collect data.
traps: 'Correlation implies causation' is a trap — it does not.
Experiments require manipulation of the independent variable.

notes.t: A research method where the researcher manipulates one or more independent variables to observe their effect on a dependent variable, often conducted in controlled environments.
A statistical technique used to measure the relationship between two or more variables. It indicates the strength and direction of a relationship but does not imply causation.

r: Structured set of open or closed questions
Direct interaction; verbal responses to pre-defined questions
Observer bias, cannot study internal processes

notes.t: Correlation indicates relationship but not causation. An experiment manipulates variables to establish cause-and-effect. Questionnaire, interview and observation are non-experimental data collection methods.
Correlation ≠ causation is a frequently tested UGC NET point. Experiments establish causality through variable manipulation and control.

mnemonics.title: QIOC
mnemonics.text: Q — Questionnaire, I — Interview, O — Observation, C — Correlation
